title: EPIC: Project Foundation
description:
## Overview
Core infrastructure and setup required before any feature development can begin. This epic establishes the SwiftData models, persistence layer, and app architecture that all other features depend on.

## Background & Rationale
BookQuotes uses the MV (Model-View) pattern with SwiftUI and SwiftData. This foundation must be rock-solid because every feature—from book registration to quote export—depends on these core models and services.

We're targeting iOS 17+ with iOS 26 Liquid Glass preparation. The architecture must support offline-first operation and eventual iCloud sync.

## Key Deliverables
1. Xcode project structure following feature-based organization
2. SwiftData models: Book, Quote, Collection, Tag, MarkingDefinition
3. ModelContainer configuration with CloudKit schema
4. Design system tokens (colors, typography, spacing)
5. Basic tab navigation shell

## Files
- BookQuotes/App/BookQuotesApp.swift
- BookQuotes/App/ContentView.swift
- BookQuotes/Models/*.swift
- BookQuotes/Components/DesignSystem.swift

## Technical Considerations
- SwiftData requires iOS 17+; we're committed to this minimum
- CloudKit sync configuration happens at ModelContainer level
- Design tokens should support both light/dark mode and Liquid Glass adaptation
- Tab navigation will use NavigationStack with per-tab routing

## Acceptance Criteria
- App builds and runs on iOS 17+ simulator/device
- All SwiftData models compile with proper relationships
- Tab bar shows all 4 tabs (Library, Capture, Search, Settings)
- Design system exports are usable across all views

## Dependencies
None - this is the foundation epic
close_reason: All foundation tasks complete: Xcode project, SwiftData models (Book, Quote, Collection, Tag, MarkingDefinition), ModelContainer config, design system tokens, TabView navigation. iOS app foundation ready for feature development.

title: Implement Book SwiftData model
description:
## Task
Implement the Book SwiftData model with all required properties and relationships.

## Why This Matters
The Book model is central to the app. Every quote belongs to a book, and the library displays books. Getting this model right sets up success for everything else.

## Implementation Details

### Model Properties
```swift
@Model
final class Book {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var title: String
    var author: String
    var isbn: String?
    var publisher: String?
    var publishYear: Int?
    var genre: String?
    var coverImageData: Data?
    var dateAdded: Date
    var dateLastQuoteAdded: Date?
    
    @Relationship(deleteRule: .cascade, inverse: \Quote.book)
    var quotes: [Quote]
    
    @Relationship(inverse: \Collection.books)
    var collections: [Collection]
    
    @Relationship(inverse: \Tag.books)
    var tags: [Tag]
}
```

### Key Design Decisions
1. Cover image stored as Data (JPEG compressed) not URL - ensures offline access
2. Cascade delete for quotes - when book deleted, its quotes go too
3. Optional fields for metadata that might not extract

### Files
- BookQuotes/Models/Book.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- Model compiles without errors
- Relationships are bidirectional
- Default values set appropriately
- Convenience initializer for quick creation
close_reason: Completed

## Task
Implement the Quote SwiftData model - the core data type of the app.

## Why This Matters
Quotes are what users are capturing. This model must handle all the metadata: text, page number, marking type, margin notes, confidence scores, and relationships.

## Implementation Details

### Model Properties
```swift
@Model
final class Quote {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var text: String
    var pageNumber: Int?
    var marginNote: String?
    var markingType: MarkingType
    var customMarkingDefinition: MarkingDefinition?
    var confidence: Double?
    var sourceImagePath: String?
    var dateAdded: Date
    var dateModified: Date?
    var isFavorite: Bool
    
    var book: Book?
    
    @Relationship(inverse: \Tag.quotes)
    var tags: [Tag]
}

enum MarkingType: String, Codable, CaseIterable {
    case underline, doubleUnderline, marginLine
    case highlight, bracket, circle
    case asterisk, questionMark, marginNote
}
```

### Key Design Decisions
1. Both legacy enum and new custom marking definition supported
2. Confidence stored for quality analytics
3. Source image path for reference (not Data to save space)
4. Favorites flag for quick filtering

title: Configure ModelContainer with CloudKit preparation
description:
## Task
Configure ModelContainer with all models and CloudKit schema preparation.

## Why This Matters
The ModelContainer is the central persistence coordinator. Proper configuration ensures all models work together and prepares for iCloud sync.

## Implementation Details

### ModelContainer Setup
```swift
@main
struct BookQuotesApp: App {
    let container: ModelContainer
    
    init() {
        let schema = Schema([
            Book.self,
            Quote.self,
            Collection.self,
            Tag.self,
            MarkingDefinition.self
        ])
        
        let config = ModelConfiguration(
            "BookQuotes",
            schema: schema,
            isStoredInMemoryOnly: false,
            cloudKitDatabase: .private("iCloud.com.yourapp.BookQuotes")
        )
        
        container = try! ModelContainer(for: schema, configurations: [config])
    }
}
```

### Key Considerations
1. CloudKit database name must match entitlements
2. Schema includes all @Model types
3. Preview container uses in-memory for SwiftUI previews
4. Migration strategy for schema changes

### Files
- BookQuotes/App/BookQuotesApp.swift
- BookQuotes/App/ModelContainerPreview.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- App launches without persistence errors
- All models can be inserted and fetched
- Preview helper works for SwiftUI previews

description:
## Task
End-to-end UI tests for book registration including camera capture of cover, OCR extraction, and manual editing.

## Testing Strategy
- Use XCUITest for full UI automation
- Test the complete book registration journey
- Handle camera permission variations
- Log all interactions and state changes

## Test Coverage

### BookRegistrationFlowTests
```swift
import XCTest

final class BookRegistrationFlowTests: XCTestCase {
    var app: XCUIApplication!
    var logger: TestLogger!
    
    override func setUp() {
        super.setUp()
        continueAfterFailure = false
        
        app = XCUIApplication()
        app.launchArguments = ["--uitesting", "--with-test-api-key"]
        logger = TestLogger(testName: name)
        
        logger.info("Launching app with test configuration")
        app.launch()
    }
    
    override func tearDown() {
        print(logger.summary())
        super.tearDown()
    }
    
    // MARK: - Navigation Tests
    
    func testLibraryTab_TapAddBook_ShowsAddOptions() throws {
        logger.step(1, "Navigating to Library tab")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Tapping add book button")
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        
        logger.step(3, "Verifying add options")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["Scan Book Cover"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["Enter Manually"].exists)
        
        logger.success("Add book options displayed")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Manual Entry Tests
    
    func testManualEntry_EnterBookDetails_SavesBook() throws {
        logger.step(1, "Navigating to manual entry")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Enter Manually"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Entering book title")
        let titleField = app.textFields["Book Title"]
        XCTAssertTrue(titleField.waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        titleField.tap()
        titleField.typeText("Test Book Title")
        
        logger.step(3, "Entering author")
        let authorField = app.textFields["Author"]
        authorField.tap()
        authorField.typeText("Test Author")
        
        logger.step(4, "Saving book")
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        
        logger.step(5, "Verifying book appears in library")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Test Book Title"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Test Author"].exists)
        
        logger.success("Manual book entry saved successfully")
    }
    
    func testManualEntry_EmptyTitle_ShowsError() throws {
        logger.step(1, "Navigating to manual entry")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Enter Manually"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Trying to save without title")
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        
        logger.step(3, "Verifying error")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts.matching(
            NSPredicate(format: "label CONTAINS 'title is required'")
        ).count > 0)
        
        logger.success("Empty title error displayed")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Camera Capture Tests (Simulated)
    
    func testCameraCapture_WithMockImage_ExtractsDetails() throws {
        // Using simulated camera with test images
        app.launchArguments.append("--mock-camera")
        app.terminate()
        app.launch()
        
        logger.step(1, "Navigating to cover scan")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Scan Book Cover"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Simulating capture")
        // Mock camera should auto-capture test image
        app.buttons["Capture"].tap()
        
        logger.step(3, "Waiting for OCR processing")
        let processingIndicator = app.activityIndicators.firstMatch
        // Wait for processing to complete (max 10 seconds)
        let startTime = Date()
        while processingIndicator.exists && Date().timeIntervalSince(startTime) < 10 {
            Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: 0.5)
        }
        
        logger.step(4, "Verifying extracted details")
        // Should show edit form with extracted data
        let titleField = app.textFields["Book Title"]
        XCTAssertTrue(titleField.waitForExistence(timeout: 5))
        
        // Title should be pre-filled from OCR
        let titleValue = titleField.value as? String ?? ""
        logger.debug("Extracted title: \(titleValue)")
        
        logger.success("Book details extracted from cover")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Edit After Capture Tests
    
    func testEditAfterCapture_CorrectTitle_SavesEdits() throws {
        app.launchArguments.append("--mock-camera")
        app.terminate()
        app.launch()
        
        logger.step(1, "Capturing book cover")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Scan Book Cover"].tap()
        app.buttons["Capture"].tap()
        
        // Wait for processing
        _ = app.textFields["Book Title"].waitForExistence(timeout: 10)
        
        logger.step(2, "Editing extracted title")
        let titleField = app.textFields["Book Title"]
        titleField.tap()
        // Clear and re-enter
        titleField.buttons["Clear text"].tap()
        titleField.typeText("Corrected Book Title")
        
        logger.step(3, "Saving edits")
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        
        logger.step(4, "Verifying corrected title in library")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Corrected Book Title"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        
        logger.success("Edited title saved correctly")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Retry/Cancel Tests
    
    func testCameraCapture_Cancel_ReturnsToLibrary() throws {
        logger.step(1, "Starting cover scan")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Scan Book Cover"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Cancelling capture")
        app.buttons["Cancel"].tap()
        
        logger.step(3, "Verifying returned to library")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].isSelected)
        
        logger.success("Cancel returns to library")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Duplicate Detection Tests
    
    func testAddBook_DuplicateTitle_ShowsWarning() throws {
        logger.step(1, "Adding first book")
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Enter Manually"].tap()
        
        let titleField = app.textFields["Book Title"]
        titleField.tap()
        titleField.typeText("Duplicate Test Book")
        
        let authorField = app.textFields["Author"]
        authorField.tap()
        authorField.typeText("Same Author")
        
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        _ = app.staticTexts["Duplicate Test Book"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3)
        
        logger.step(2, "Adding duplicate book")
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Enter Manually"].tap()
        
        app.textFields["Book Title"].tap()
        app.textFields["Book Title"].typeText("Duplicate Test Book")
        app.textFields["Author"].tap()
        app.textFields["Author"].typeText("Same Author")
        
        logger.step(3, "Saving duplicate")
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        
        logger.step(4, "Verifying duplicate warning")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.alerts.firstMatch.waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.alerts.staticTexts.matching(
            NSPredicate(format: "label CONTAINS 'already exists' OR label CONTAINS 'duplicate'")
        ).count > 0)
        
        logger.success("Duplicate warning shown")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Book Detail View Tests
    
    func testTapBook_ShowsDetailView() throws {
        // Add a book first
        try addTestBook(title: "Detail Test Book", author: "Test Author")
        
        logger.step(1, "Tapping on book")
        app.staticTexts["Detail Test Book"].tap()
        
        logger.step(2, "Verifying detail view")
        XCTAssertTrue(app.navigationBars["Detail Test Book"].waitForExistence(timeout: 3))
        XCTAssertTrue(app.staticTexts["Test Author"].exists)
        XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["Add Quote"].exists)
        
        logger.success("Book detail view displays correctly")
    }
    
    // MARK: - Helpers
    
    private func addTestBook(title: String, author: String) throws {
        app.tabBars.buttons["Library"].tap()
        app.buttons["Add Book"].tap()
        app.buttons["Enter Manually"].tap()
        
        app.textFields["Book Title"].tap()
        app.textFields["Book Title"].typeText(title)
        app.textFields["Author"].tap()
        app.textFields["Author"].typeText(author)
        app.buttons["Save"].tap()
        
        _ = app.staticTexts[title].waitForExistence(timeout: 3)
    }
}
```

### Files

- [ ] Empty title shows error
- [ ] Camera capture extracts details

description:
## Overview
User-defined annotation vocabulary system that personalizes AI extraction. Every reader marks books differently; this feature teaches the AI each user's unique system.

## Background & Rationale
Some readers use single underlines for important passages, double underlines for critical ones, wavy lines for disagreement, asterisks for action items, question marks for research needed. The generic extraction approach misses this semantic richness.

By defining their marking vocabulary, users get:
1. More accurate extraction (AI knows what to look for)
2. Semantic categorization (marking type conveys meaning)
3. Personalized organization (filter quotes by marking type)

## Key Deliverables
1. MarkingDefinition SwiftData model
2. System default markings (underline, highlight, margin line, etc.)
3. Custom marking creation/editing UI
4. Dynamic prompt generation incorporating user's vocabulary
5. Onboarding templates (Academic, Creative, Business, Standard)
6. Quote-to-marking association

## Files
- BookQuotes/Models/MarkingDefinition.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Settings/MarkingDefinitionsView.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Settings/MarkingDefinitionEditor.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Onboarding/MarkingTemplateSelector.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/GeminiService+PromptBuilder.swift

## Technical Considerations
- Visual descriptions must be clear enough for AI to identify in images
- Semantic meanings help with categorization but aren't used in extraction
- Migration path from legacy MarkingType enum to custom definitions
- System defaults can be edited but not deleted
- Sort order matters for prompt construction

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can create custom marking with name, visual description, meaning
- System defaults are pre-populated on first launch
- Onboarding offers template selection
- Custom markings appear in extraction prompts
- Quotes display their marking type with appropriate styling

EPIC: Backend & Subscriptions
description:
## Overview
Lightweight backend infrastructure for API proxying, user authentication, and subscription management. Enables seamless UX without users needing their own API keys.

## Background & Rationale
Consumer apps need frictionless onboarding. Requiring users to obtain API keys, add credit cards to Google, and manage quotas is a non-starter for non-technical users. A simple proxy server with subscription validation solves this.

The economics are favorable: Gemini 2.5 Flash costs ~$0.001 per page extraction. Even heavy users (1000 pages/month) cost ~$1. A $5/month subscription has 80%+ margin.

## Architecture
```
iOS App → Your Proxy Server → Gemini API
              ↓
         Validates:
         - Apple Sign-In JWT
         - Subscription status
         - Usage limits
```

## Key Deliverables
1. Serverless proxy (Cloudflare Workers / Vercel Edge / AWS Lambda)
2. Apple Sign-In authentication
3. StoreKit 2 subscription handling
4. Usage tracking and rate limiting
5. Subscription status sync

## Technical Considerations
- Serverless = near-zero cost at low scale, auto-scales
- Apple Sign-In provides user identity without email/password
- StoreKit 2 server notifications for subscription status
- Could use simple KV storage (no complex database needed)
- Proxy adds ~50-100ms latency (acceptable for this use case)

## Cost Projections
- Cloudflare Workers: Free tier = 100k req/day, $5/mo = 10M req
- Gemini API: ~$0.001/extraction
- 1000 users × 100 extractions/month = $100 Gemini cost
- Revenue at $5/user = $5000/month (50:1 ratio)

## Dependencies
None - this is foundational for the subscription model

description:
## Task
Create a shared ImagePreprocessor/ImageUtilities module that prepares captured images for Gemini requests.

## Why This Matters
Consistent preprocessing improves extraction quality and keeps payload sizes predictable, reducing latency and cost. It should be shared by both cover and quote capture flows.

## Implementation Details
- Normalize orientation (EXIF).
- Resize longest edge to max ~2048px (configurable).
- JPEG encode at 0.75–0.85 quality.
- Optional light contrast/brightness adjustment (behind a flag).
- Return `Data` plus basic metadata (size, compression ratio).

## Files
- BookQuotes/Utilities/ImagePreprocessor.swift (or ImageUtilities.swift)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Utilities can preprocess a `UIImage` and return JPEG `Data`.
- Output respects max dimension and quality settings.
- Both book cover and quote capture flows can call the same preprocessing entry point.

description:
## Overview
Offline-first architecture enabling users to capture photos anywhere, with automatic processing when connectivity returns.

## Background & Rationale
Reading happens everywhere—planes, beaches, cabins, commutes. Users shouldn't have to wait for WiFi to capture their annotations. The offline queue stores captured images locally and processes them automatically when the device reconnects.

This transforms BookQuotes from a "connected tool" to a "capture anywhere" app. Users can photograph an entire book's annotations during a flight and have them all processed upon landing.

## Key Deliverables
1. CaptureQueueItem SwiftData model with status tracking
2. CaptureQueueManager service with NWPathMonitor
3. Background processing with progress tracking
4. Queue status UI showing pending/processing/failed items
5. Retry logic with exponential backoff
6. Error handling with user-friendly messages

- BookQuotes/Services/CaptureQueueManager.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/NetworkMonitor.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Library/QueueStatusView.swift

## Technical Considerations
- NWPathMonitor for reliable network state detection
- Images stored in app's Documents directory, not SwiftData (too large)
- Background app refresh for processing when app is backgrounded
- Memory management for large image queues
- Clear distinction between capture date and processing date

## Acceptance Criteria
- Photos captured offline are persisted across app restarts
- Processing begins automatically when network available
- Queue UI shows accurate status for each item
- Failed items can be manually retried
- Successfully processed items are cleaned up

When offline, captured images must be stored persistently so they survive app restarts and process when connectivity returns.

}

description:
## Overview
Complete system for registering books via cover photo capture or ISBN barcode scanning. This is the entry point for users adding books to their library.

## Background & Rationale
Users need a fast, accurate way to add books. Cover photo OCR works well but can fail with damaged covers or unusual fonts. ISBN barcode scanning provides near-100% accuracy as a reliable fallback.

The dual-method approach ensures users can always add books regardless of cover condition. AI extracts metadata (title, author, publisher, year, genre) from cover images, while barcode lookup provides authoritative data from Google Books/OpenLibrary APIs.

## Key Deliverables
1. Cover photo capture with camera preview
2. Gemini API integration for cover metadata extraction
3. ISBN barcode scanner using Vision framework
4. Google Books & OpenLibrary API clients
5. Manual metadata editing interface
6. Book detail view with edit capabilities

- BookQuotes/Services/ISBNLookupService.swift

## Technical Considerations
- AVFoundation for camera access; requires NSCameraUsageDescription
- VNDetectBarcodesRequest with EAN-13/UPC-A symbologies for ISBN
- ISBN validation: check digit verification for ISBN-10 and ISBN-13
- Google Books API is free but rate-limited; OpenLibrary is fallback
- Cover images should be resized before sending to Gemini (1024px max)

## Acceptance Criteria
- User can capture book cover and see extracted metadata
- User can scan ISBN barcode with immediate metadata lookup
- Extracted metadata is editable before saving
- Books appear in library immediately after registration
- Works offline (queues for later processing)

title: Implement cover metadata extraction prompt
description:
## Task
Implement the cover photo analysis prompt and response parsing for book metadata extraction.

## Why This Matters
The prompt engineering determines extraction quality. A well-crafted prompt extracts title, author, publisher, year, and genre from cover photos accurately.

## Implementation Details

### Extraction Prompt
```swift
extension GeminiService {
    func extractBookMetadata(from imageData: Data) async throws -> BookMetadata {
        let prompt = """
        Analyze this book cover image and extract metadata.
        
        Return a JSON object with these fields:
        {
          "title": "The exact book title",
          "author": "Author name(s)",
          "subtitle": "Subtitle if present, or null",
          "publisher": "Publisher name if visible, or null",
          "publishYear": 2023 or null,
          "genre": "Best guess at genre",
          "confidence": 0.95
        }
        
        Rules:
        1. Extract the EXACT title as printed
        2. For multiple authors, use comma separation
        3. Genre should be single category (Fiction, Non-Fiction, etc.)
        4. confidence is 0.0-1.0 for overall extraction quality
        
        Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown.
        """
        
        let response = try await generateContent(prompt: prompt, image: imageData)
        return try parseBookMetadata(from: response)
    }
}

struct BookMetadata: Codable {
    let title: String
    let author: String
    let subtitle: String?
    let publisher: String?
    let publishYear: Int?
    let genre: String?
    let confidence: Double
}
```

### Files
- BookQuotes/Services/GeminiService+BookMetadata.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/BookMetadata.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- Prompt extracts all metadata fields
- JSON parsing handles missing optional fields
- Confidence score returned
- Works with various cover styles

title: EPIC: Quote Capture
description:
## Overview
The heart of BookQuotes: capturing photos of marked book pages and extracting underlined passages, highlights, and margin notes using AI.

## Background & Rationale
Users mark up physical books in countless ways—underlines, highlights, margin lines, brackets, circles, margin notes. The AI must identify these visual markers and extract the marked text accurately.

Image quality is critical for extraction success. Blurry photos, poor lighting, or skewed angles cause failures. Pre-upload quality assessment prevents wasted API calls and user frustration.

Multi-page batch capture lets users photograph many pages in succession, then process them together. This is essential for digitizing an entire book's annotations efficiently.

## Key Deliverables
1. Page capture camera with quality feedback overlay
2. Image quality analyzer (blur, brightness, text confidence)
3. Multi-page batch capture session management
4. Gemini API quote extraction with custom marking vocabulary
5. Quote review/edit interface post-extraction
6. Page number detection and association

- BookQuotes/Services/QuoteExtractionService.swift
- BookQuotes/Models/CaptureSession.swift

## Technical Considerations
- Vision framework VNRecognizeTextRequest for text presence detection
- CIImage filters for blur detection (Laplacian variance method)
- CIAreaAverage for brightness analysis
- Batch processing should show progress and allow cancellation
- Memory management critical for multi-page sessions (10-20 images)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Quality overlay shows real-time feedback during capture
- Poor quality images are rejected with actionable advice

## Task

Users often want to capture many pages at once. The CaptureSession groups related captures and tracks batch processing state.

```swift
@Model
final class CaptureSession {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var book: Book
    var dateStarted: Date
    var dateCompleted: Date?
    var status: SessionStatus
    var totalPages: Int

        case pending, processing, completed, failed
    }
}
```

title: Implement dynamic quote extraction prompt builder
description:
## Task
Implement dynamic quote extraction prompt that incorporates user's custom marking vocabulary.

## Why This Matters
Each user marks books differently. The prompt must be personalized to look for their specific marking types to achieve accurate extraction.

## Implementation Details

### Dynamic Prompt Builder
```swift
extension GeminiService {
    func buildQuoteExtractionPrompt(markings: [MarkingDefinition]) -> String {
        let enabledMarkings = markings.filter { \$0.isEnabled }
        
        let markingDescriptions = enabledMarkings.map { marking in
            """
            - **\(marking.name)**: \(marking.visualDescription)
              Meaning: \(marking.meaning)
            """
        }.joined(separator: "\n")
        
        let markingTypes = enabledMarkings.map {
            "\"\(\$0.name.lowercased().replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "_"))\""
        }.joined(separator: " | ")
        
        return """
        Analyze this book page image to extract marked/highlighted passages.
        
        The reader uses the following marking system:
        
        \(markingDescriptions)
        
        Return a JSON object:
        {
          "quotes": [
            {
              "text": "The exact text that was marked",
              "pageNumber": 42,
              "marginNote": "Any handwritten note near this passage, or null",
              "markingType": \(markingTypes),
              "confidence": 0.92
            }
          ],
          "pageNumber": 42,
          "processingNotes": "Optional notes about extraction quality"
        }
        
        Rules:
        1. Extract COMPLETE marked passage - include full sentences
        2. Match marking type to user's vocabulary above
        3. If multiple marking types, use the primary one
        4. Preserve original formatting where meaningful
        5. Transcribe handwritten margin notes accurately
        6. Include page number if visible
        7. Separate passages = separate quote objects
        8. confidence 0.0-1.0 for each quote's accuracy
        
        Respond with ONLY valid JSON, no markdown.
        """
    }
    
    func extractQuotes(from imageData: Data, markings: [MarkingDefinition]) async throws -> QuoteExtractionResult
}
```

### Files
- BookQuotes/Services/GeminiService+QuoteExtraction.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/QuoteExtractionResult.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- Prompt includes all enabled marking definitions
- User's visual descriptions guide extraction
- Response parses into structured result
- Confidence scores returned per quote

EPIC: Testing & Quality Assurance
description:
## Epic Overview
Comprehensive testing infrastructure ensuring BookQuotes is reliable, performant, and regression-free.

## Testing Philosophy

### No Mocks - Real Implementations Only
We test real code with real dependencies configured for testing:
- **SwiftData**: In-memory `ModelContainer` with `isStoredInMemoryOnly: true`
- **SQLite FTS5**: Temporary database files in `FileManager.temporaryDirectory`
- **Network**: Test API keys with recorded responses (not fake services)
- **Camera**: Simulated with real image data, not mock capture sessions

### Swift 6.2+ Concurrency Patterns
- `@MainActor` test classes for UI-bound services
- `async` test methods with proper `await`
- Actor isolation respected in test setup/teardown
- `@concurrent` functions tested for off-main-actor execution

### Test Categories

| Category | Purpose | Count |
|----------|---------|-------|
| **Unit Tests** | Individual components in isolation | ~25 |
| **Integration Tests** | Component interactions | ~10 |
| **E2E UI Tests** | Full user flows with logging | ~8 |
| **Performance Tests** | Speed and memory benchmarks | ~5 |

## Directory Structure
```
BookQuotesTests/
├── Infrastructure/
│   ├── TestLogger.swift
│   ├── TestFixtures.swift
│   ├── SwiftDataTestCase.swift
│   └── FTS5TestCase.swift
├── Unit/
│   ├── Models/
│   ├── Services/
│   └── Utilities/
├── Integration/
│   ├── CaptureFlowTests.swift
│   ├── SearchFlowTests.swift
│   └── OfflineQueueFlowTests.swift
└── Performance/
    ├── SearchPerformanceTests.swift
    └── LargeDatasetTests.swift

BookQuotesUITests/
├── Infrastructure/
│   ├── UITestLogger.swift
│   ├── ScreenshotCapture.swift
│   └── BaseUITestCase.swift
├── Flows/
│   ├── OnboardingFlowTests.swift
│   ├── BookRegistrationFlowTests.swift
│   ├── QuoteCaptureFlowTests.swift
│   └── SearchFlowTests.swift
└── TestPlans/
    └── FullRegressionPlan.xctestplan
```

## Coverage Targets
- **Line Coverage**: 80%+ for Services, 70%+ for Views
- **Branch Coverage**: 75%+ for critical paths
- **All public APIs**: 100% tested

## Subtasks Overview
1. Test Infrastructure (logging, fixtures, base classes)
2. Model Unit Tests (Book, Quote, MarkingDefinition, etc.)
3. Service Unit Tests (SearchService, GeminiService, etc.)
4. Utility Unit Tests (Levenshtein, tokenization, etc.)

title: EPIC: Data Quality
description:
## Overview
Systems ensuring quote accuracy through duplicate detection, confidence scoring, and correction feedback loops that improve future extractions.

## Background & Rationale
AI extraction isn't perfect. Users will correct errors—and those corrections are valuable training signals. Confidence scores help users identify quotes that may need review. Duplicate detection prevents accidentally saving the same quote twice from different capture sessions.

Together, these features transform a basic OCR tool into a learning system that gets better over time and maintains data integrity.

## Key Deliverables
1. DuplicateDetector service with fuzzy string matching
2. Levenshtein distance algorithm implementation
3. ConfidenceIndicator UI component
4. QuoteCorrection model for tracking edits
5. Duplicate warning UI before save
6. Quote editing with correction tracking
7. Statistics on correction patterns

## Files
- BookQuotes/Services/DuplicateDetector.swift
- BookQuotes/Utilities/LevenshteinDistance.swift
- BookQuotes/Models/QuoteCorrection.swift
- BookQuotes/Components/ConfidenceIndicator.swift
- BookQuotes/Components/DuplicateWarningSheet.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Library/QuoteEditView.swift

## Technical Considerations
- Levenshtein distance is O(mn); consider optimization for long quotes
- 85% similarity threshold balances false positives/negatives
- Confidence scores come from Gemini API; store for analytics
- Corrections should store both original and edited text
- Deduplication should check across all books, not just current

## Acceptance Criteria
- Duplicate quotes are detected before saving
- User sees warning with original quote for comparison
- Confidence scores display visually (color-coded dots/bars)
- Quote edits are tracked with before/after
- Correction statistics available in settings

description:
## Task
Build ConfidenceIndicator UI component for visual display of extraction confidence scores.

## Why This Matters
Confidence scores help users identify quotes that may need review. Visual indicators make this information scannable.

## Implementation Details

### ConfidenceIndicator
```swift
struct ConfidenceIndicator: View {
    let confidence: Double
    let style: IndicatorStyle
    
    enum IndicatorStyle {
        case dot, bar, badge
    }
    
    var color: Color {
        switch confidence {
        case 0.9...: return .green
        case 0.7..<0.9: return .yellow
        case 0.5..<0.7: return .orange
        default: return .red
        }
    }
    
    var label: String {
        switch confidence {
        case 0.9...: return "High"
        case 0.7..<0.9: return "Good"
        case 0.5..<0.7: return "Fair"
        default: return "Low"
        }
    }
    
    var body: some View {
        switch style {
        case .dot:
            Circle()
                .fill(color)
                .frame(width: 8, height: 8)
        
        case .bar:
            GeometryReader { geo in
                ZStack(alignment: .leading) {
                    Rectangle()
                        .fill(Color.secondary.opacity(0.2))
                    Rectangle()
                        .fill(color)
                        .frame(width: geo.size.width * confidence)
                }
            }
            .frame(height: 4)
            .clipShape(Capsule())
        
        case .badge:
            Text(label)
                .font(.caption2)
                .padding(.horizontal, 6)
                .padding(.vertical, 2)
                .background(color.opacity(0.2))
                .foregroundStyle(color)
                .clipShape(Capsule())
        }
    }
}
```

### Usage
```swift
// In quote card
HStack {
    Text(quote.text)
    Spacer()
    ConfidenceIndicator(confidence: quote.confidence ?? 1.0, style: .dot)
}

// In detail view
ConfidenceIndicator(confidence: quote.confidence ?? 1.0, style: .bar)
```

### Files
- BookQuotes/Components/ConfidenceIndicator.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- Three style variants work correctly
- Color thresholds are visually distinct
- Works with nil confidence (defaults to 1.0)
- Accessible with VoiceOver labels

title: Implement QuoteCorrection tracking model
description:
## Task
Implement QuoteCorrection model for tracking user edits to improve future extraction accuracy.

## Why This Matters
User corrections are valuable training signals. Tracking what users change helps identify extraction patterns that need improvement.

## Implementation Details

### QuoteCorrection Model
```swift
@Model
final class QuoteCorrection {
    @Attribute(.unique) var id: UUID
    var quote: Quote
    var originalText: String
    var correctedText: String
    var correctionType: CorrectionType
    var dateCreated: Date
    
    enum CorrectionType: String, Codable {
        case textEdit       // Modified quote text
        case pageNumber     // Changed page number
        case markingType    // Changed marking type
        case marginNote     // Changed margin note
        case deletion       // Deleted incorrect quote
        case addition       // Manually added quote
    }
    
    init(quote: Quote, originalText: String, correctedText: String, type: CorrectionType) {
        self.id = UUID()
        self.quote = quote
        self.originalText = originalText
        self.correctedText = correctedText
        self.correctionType = type
        self.dateCreated = Date()
    }
}
```

### Correction Tracking
```swift
extension Quote {
    func recordCorrection(original: String, corrected: String, type: CorrectionType, context: ModelContext) {
        let correction = QuoteCorrection(
            quote: self,
            originalText: original,
            correctedText: corrected,
            type: type
        )
        context.insert(correction)
        self.dateModified = Date()
    }
}
```

### Files
- BookQuotes/Models/QuoteCorrection.swift

## Acceptance Criteria
- Model captures before/after state
- Correction type categorizes changes
- Relationship to quote maintained
- Statistics can be computed from corrections

title: EPIC: Export System
description:
## Overview
Multi-format export enabling users to share their quote collections with external tools: Markdown, Plain Text, JSON, Notion, and Obsidian.

## Background & Rationale
Quote collections gain value when integrated into users' existing workflows. Knowledge workers use Notion; writers use Obsidian; developers want JSON. Local backup ensures data isn't trapped in the app.

Each format has specific requirements:
- Markdown: Human-readable, universally supported
- Plain Text: Simplest, works everywhere
- JSON: Machine-readable, full metadata preserved
- Notion: API-based direct sync with databases
- Obsidian: Markdown files in vault with YAML frontmatter

## Key Deliverables
1. ExportService with format-specific formatters
2. MarkdownFormatter with attribution blocks
3. NotionExporter with API integration
4. ObsidianFormatter with YAML frontmatter
5. Export UI with format selection and preview
6. Local backup to Files app
7. Share sheet integration

## Files
- BookQuotes/Services/ExportService.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/Exporters/MarkdownFormatter.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/Exporters/NotionExporter.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/Exporters/ObsidianFormatter.swift
- BookQuotes/Services/BackupService.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Export/ExportView.swift
- BookQuotes/Features/Export/ExportPreviewView.swift

## Technical Considerations
- Notion API requires OAuth or integration token; store in Keychain
- Obsidian vault path detection varies by platform
- Large exports should use streaming to avoid memory issues
- Share sheet UIActivityViewController for iOS integration
- Files app export uses UIDocumentPickerViewController

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 5 export formats produce valid, well-formatted output
- User can preview export before executing
- Notion export creates/updates pages in specified database
- Obsidian export generates vault-ready markdown files
- Local backup creates timestamped JSON in Files app
- Share sheet allows sending to any compatible app

## Dependencies
Depends on: EPIC: Project Foundation, EPIC: Library UI (need quotes to export)
